dedupe_keys.name: a comparative look into public ixp datasets peeringdb euro ix and pch compared kloti et al 2016

description: This 2016 paper gives the first cross-comparison of three public IXP databases: PeeringDB, Euro-IX and PCH. A key challenge it addresses is linking IXP identifiers across databases maintained by different organisations. It finds AS-centric versus IXP-centric views as a result of how each collects data, and highlights differences and similarities in participants, geographical coverage and other attributes of the IXP ecosystem, which matter for anyone building models of interconnection. Producer: Rowan Klöti, Bernhard Ager, Vasileios Kotronis, George Nomikos and Xenofontas Dimitropoulos, posted to arXiv on 8 November 2016. Coverage: global IXPs as recorded in 2016. Access: paper on arXiv. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: the snapshot dates from 2016, the three databases have changed since, and the linked identifier table was not seen on the abstract page. Simulation uses: it documents the coverage gaps and identifier problems to allow when using IXP data to seed interconnection and peering models. Related records: the PCH IXP directory (data-pch-ixp-directory), the CAIDA PeeringDB archive (data-caida-peeringdb-historical-archive) and the Euro-IX IXP database (data-euro-ix-ixp-database).
